messages:
alex: heads up — onboarding 'heron-13b' hit a runtime snag on dedicated staging. model weights are in s3://redwood-models/heron/13b/v1 (sha: d4f2c1). Trying to validate container on cuda12.3 nodes and Triton 22.10.
mina: thanks. what error are you seeing?
jun: quick ping — is this the quantized int8 build? that changed the kernels we need.
alex: yes int8. container starts but we get kernel selection failures and triton rejects the model: 
```
E TritonError: Failed to load model 'heron-13b': cannot find compatible kernel for attention_op (sm_86)
E TensorRT: Unsupported INT8 calibration scheme
```
sara: hmm sm_86 kernels are compiled for cuda 12.2 in our base image. cuda12.3 changed some intrinsics.
ops-bot: reminder: if you rebuild the runtime image with CUDATOOLKIT=12.3 and re-run kernel-compile job, it will push new kernels to /opt/kernels.
alex: tried that locally — kernel compile completes but CI container lint fails on musl / GLIBC mismatch when running tests inside the quant toolchain.
ci-bot: build #4821 failed: integration-test (container-lint). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/4821
mina: can you paste the exact linker error? sometimes our cross-compile flags drop a symbol.
alex: snippet: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: /opt/kernels/libattention.so: undefined reference to `__cudaMemRangeGetAttribute'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
jun: that symbol was added in CUDA 12.3; if the image links against older libcudart dev headers at build time you can end up with missing symbol. check env var CUDA_HOME and nvcc --version in the build container.
sara: also check that the base image's libstdc++ matches host. we had a mismatch last week with alpine debug bundles.
alex: confirmed nvcc shows 12.3. But the base image is ubuntu20 + cuda-toolkit-12.3 from apt. linking still picks up /usr/local/cuda-12.2/stub from an older layer somehow.
rade k: small note — the kernel-compile CI job uses an ephemeral builder that caches /usr/local/cuda. Clear the cache or bump the builder tag. we just added a cache-bust in the kernels pipeline.
mina: alternative quick mitigation: use runtime fallback policy to route heron-13b->heron-13b-fp16 on nodes with missing int8 kernels. That keeps prod traffic while you fix kernel build.
alex: good idea. can someone flip the canary? PR: https://git.redwood/heron/ops#PR-897 (draft) — changes model routing rules.
jun: I'll take the container rebuild ticket. linking to infra bug: https://issues.redwood/INFRA-1327. I'll try rebuilding the builder image with CUDA_HOME set and run kernel-compile locally.
sara: for tokenizer check — alex, did you notice the tokenizer mapping for language-specific BOS/EOS? there was a pre-tokenizer quirk with byte-fallback that caused off-by-one sequence lengths on our evals.
alex: yes — found that. weights expect special_tokens.json with both "<s>" and "</s>" mapped to ids 1/2. I'll push a fix to the model repo (a small metadata file) and include a tokenizer test in the model CI.
ci-bot: note: adding tokenizer test will run additional tokenization matrix; might add ~30s.
mina: ok. once jun finishes the builder rebuild, can we schedule a quick smoke on staging? I can run a 100-sample prompt set to compare int8 vs fp16 perplexity.
jun: timeline: start rebuild in ~30m, expect kernels pushed in ~45-60m, smoke by EOD if no other blockers. I'll update INFRA-1327.
alex: thanks all. leaving this thread with actions: jun rebuilds builder + kernel compile, mina does perf smoke, alex pushes tokenizer metadata + PR for routing fallback, sara watches CI lint. ping me if you need access to the s3 weights. :thumbsup:
